title: Chip Industry Technical Paper Roundup: Oct. 6
gist: A list of six new technical papers added to Semiconductor Engineering's library: low-contact-resistance WSe2 transistors, backside clock meshes for 2nm GAAFETs, row-parallel DRAM arithmetic (RAPID), High Bandwidth Flash for LLM serving, a formal security analysis of CAN XL, and device-to-RTL abstraction. Titles and affiliations only, no results given.

insights.claim: A paper from HUST, PolyU, UC Santa Barbara and NUS reports low contact resistance and high current density in ballistic p-type transistors based on oxygen-doped WSe2 monolayers, addressing a contact bottleneck for 2D transistors in advanced CMOS.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: 2D-channel transistors are a post-silicon scaling candidate; p-type contact resistance is a key blocker to watch.
insights.quote: Low contact resistance and high current density in ballistic p-type transistors based on oxygen-doped WSe₂ monolayers

insights.claim: UC Santa Cruz published a design-space exploration of backside clock meshes for 2nm GAAFET technology with backside power delivery (BSPDN); a related item on the page says backside clock meshes cut skew and power in 2nm nanosheets.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Backside power and clocking is becoming part of the 2nm design flow, which matters for EDA and foundry back-end suppliers.
insights.quote: Design Space Exploration of Backside Clock Meshes for 2 nm GAAFET BSPDN Technology

insights.claim: Syracuse University, FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg and TU Dresden present RAPID, row-parallel arithmetic processing in DRAM, a processing-in-memory approach.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Processing-in-DRAM remains an academic active area for relieving memory-bandwidth bottlenecks.
insights.quote: RAPID: Row-Parallel Arithmetic Processing in DRAM

insights.claim: UC Berkeley and FuriosaAI characterize High Bandwidth Flash (HBF) for LLM serving, indicating interest in flash-based high-bandwidth memory tiers for high-throughput inference.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: HBF is emerging as a proposed memory tier alongside HBM for inference; a FuriosaAI co-author shows AI chip startups are exploring it.
insights.quote: Characterizing High Bandwidth Flash for LLM Serving

insights.claim: Georgia Tech, Qatar Computing Research Institute and Purdue published a formal security analysis of CAN XL, the next-generation automotive bus.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Automotive network protocol security is receiving formal-verification attention as vehicles become software-defined.
insights.quote: A Formal Security Analysis of CAN XL

insights.claim: Infineon Technologies and TU Munich address abstraction and validation from physical devices up to RTL models in hardware engineering.
insights.speaker: Linda Christensen
insights.so_what: Industry-academia work on connecting device physics to RTL models; marginal investment signal.
insights.quote: From Physical Devices to RTL Models: Abstraction and Validation in Hardware Engineering
